title: One-level density of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions beyond support (−2,2)
credit: Özlük–Snyder (Canad. J. Math. 58, 2006; earlier 1999 work) and Rubinstein (Duke 2001) for support (−2,2); Katz–Sarnak (1999) density conjectures.
premise_risks: RH is a theorem (Alpöge, Lean library released 20 Nov 2026, certified 21 Nov 2026 by the Lean FRO/Mathlib Initiative against Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis). GRH for Dirichlet L-functions is treated as proved on the strength of Alpöge's announcement (alpo.ge/remark.pdf) and his Lean archive; the public certification names only RH, so the Dirichlet part has not yet been certified independently. Hecke, Dedekind and other L-functions remain open.
With GRH-Dirichlet proved, the (−2,2) results are unconditional; extending the support past 2 remains open.
plain: The low-lying zeros of L(s,χ_d) for quadratic characters are known to follow the symplectic random-matrix law for test functions whose Fourier transform is supported in (−2,2) (Özlük–Snyder, Rubinstein and successors). Those results assumed GRH, which Alpöge proved for Dirichlet L-functions in Nov 2026, so they now hold unconditionally. Go beyond 2.
math: For the family of real primitive characters $\chi_{8d}$, $d$ odd squarefree, $X<d\le 2X$, and even Schwartz $\phi$ with $\operatorname{supp}\hat\phi\subset(-\sigma,\sigma)$, prove, assuming GRH for Dirichlet $L$-functions (now a theorem, Alpöge 2026; kept as a hypothesis to match the Lean statement), that $\frac1{|\mathcal F|}\sum_d\sum_{\gamma_d}\phi\!\big(\gamma_d\frac{\log X}{2\pi}\big)\to\int\phi(x)\big(1-\frac{\sin 2\pi x}{2\pi x}\big)dx$ for some $\sigma>2$.
